title: Autotune surge-detection thresholds, resilient rollback procedures, and post-incident remediation
creator: Asha Menon
description: Incident follow-up and playbook focused on autotuner surge detection thresholds, safe apply/rollback choreography, and new verification gates for batching and KV cache changes. Builds on recent incidents where aggressive autotune recommendations caused transient tail-latency increases and customer-visible throttles. This ticket captures findings, procedural changes, and concrete remediation work to prevent recurrence.
executive_summary: A weekend autotune run applied aggressive batching and aggressive KV cache prefetch settings to several customer pools. The changes reduced per-token cost in steady-state but introduced momentary request backpressure when cold-hot mix shifted, causing elevated p95/p99 latency and partial request failures. Rapid rollback mitigations were performed, but gaps in surge detection and automated rollforward/rollback logic increased recovery time. This work delivers detection thresholds, pre-apply simulation checks, and a resilient rollback playbook to reduce MTTR and avoid customer impact during future autotune runs.

investigation_findings: Autotune promoted recommendations based primarily on average throughput/cost signals; tail-latency signals were underweighted in the objective function
Canary progression policy lacked an adaptive gate for simultaneous increase in queue depth and decrease in CPU headroom
Monitoring SLO thresholds for p95/p99 were too permissive for rapid config applies and had high evaluation windows (10m) delaying alerting
Rollback orchestration assumed idempotent config apply and did not account for interim cache warmup state, causing oscillation during revert
No pre-apply synthetic load simulation was performed for bursty patterns present on affected customer workloads
root_cause: Autotune objective and rollout policy combined to favor cost savings without sufficiently weighting tail-latency and queue-depth safety signals. Canary gating and monitoring latency windows were insufficient to detect rapid surges; rollback choreography did not include freeze points for KV cache warmup or in-flight request draining, which extended MTTR.
impact_metrics: ~6% of requests experienced >2x latency at p99 for 35 minutes; two high-tier customers reported degraded responses resulting in three production incidents; estimated incremental user-visible errors ~320 requests; short-term cost savings negated by SLA credits and engineering recovery time.
mitigations_applied: Immediate manual rollback of autotune changes across affected pools
Temp increase of rate-limiting headroom and emergency scaling of burst capacity for 6 hours
Raised monitoring sensitivity: lowered p95/p99 alert windows to 2m for autotune-apply streams and added queue-depth alerts
Manual throttling of future autotune promotions until safety gates validated
rollback_playbook: Step 1: Signal pause — mark autotune pipeline PAUSED and notify on-call (channel #autotune-ops)
Step 2: Block further promotions — set policy flag 'autotune.allow_promote' to false for affected orgs
Step 3: Execute selective revert: apply previous stable config to one pool, let KV cache warm for 5m, validate p95 and qdepth
Step 4: If stable, widen revert to remaining pools with 10% traffic step increases and 3m stabilization checks
Step 5: If oscillation persists, escalate to SRE lead and initiate emergency scale-out until safe state achieved
Step 6: Post-rollback, run synthetic burst tests to verify recovery and capture diagnostics
safe_apply_checks: Preflight simulation against a representative replay of 24h traffic (must complete within 15m)
Mandatory tail-latency delta check: predicted p99 delta must be <5% before promotion
Queue-depth headroom check: CPU and memory available headroom >20% for target pools
KV cache warmup window defined: autotune must include warmup directives when changing cache prefetch or eviction settings
Canary progression hold points at 5%, 25%, 60% with explicit stabilization metrics and max-delta gates
canary_plan: Introduce dynamic canary sizing based on recent traffic variance instead of fixed percentages
Add synthetic spike injection during canary to exercise burst paths
Require both canary passing and synthetic test passing before any auto-promotion
Log canary traces to dedicated index for quick diffing and automatic regression detection
postmortem_notes: Objective function reweighting: increase tail-latency penalty and add queue-depth term to autotune scoring
Improve rollout policy to evaluate short-window metrics (1–3m) alongside default longer windows
Add simulation harness to autotune pipeline as mandatory gate; implement a fast, resource-efficient replay runner
Design a 'safe revert' state machine that respects cache warmup and in-flight requests to avoid oscillatory applies
